chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: Insurance coverage that paid his hospital bills
summary: Cobb says good insurance covered his hospitalization and, from his Atlanta Life days, he stays insurance conscious for his family.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: How much were you covered by

I was covered pretty well. I had good insurance until they just stopped. But I didn't have to pay anything out of my pocket for anything. The biggest money I spent was to live at home, with expenses going on. Really, I didn't have to pay any hospital bills. I had enough coverage there.
Well. Eelen, I wrote insurance, I told you, for Atlanta Life.

And I knew the value of insurance. When a young man died, going to join Cootie Williams, then I became really insurance conscious for myself, you know. So I wanted enough coverage, and I'd get it for my family. I got it now. Now, I go in the hospital today and come out with money instead of paying money because I got a rider that pay me cash money that -- I bought that too.
My daughter can do the same thing. And this is an investment.
